entries.question: Nico controls Analia's [Bane Alley Blackguard] enchanted with their [Corrupted Conscience]. Analia casts their own [Lay Claim], targeting Nico's Corrupted Conscience. After it resolves, who controls the Bane Alley Blackguard? Who controls the Corrupted Conscience?

entries.answer:
Analia controls Analia's Bane Alley Blackguard and Analia controls Corrupted Conscience after Lay Claim resolves. 

Reasoning: When Lay Claim resolves it becomes an Aura attached to the targeted permanent (Corrupted Conscience) and is put onto the battlefield attached to that target (rules: an Aura spell becoming a permanent and attaching to its target: [608.3c]; Auras enter the battlefield attached to objects or players: [303.4]). Lay Claim’s text (“You control enchanted permanent.”) makes Analia the controller of the permanent it enchants, which is Corrupted Conscience (Lay Claim card text). Because Corrupted Conscience’s text says “You control enchanted creature,” that effect applies to the controller of Corrupted Conscience (Corrupted Conscience card text) and therefore makes Analia the controller of the creature Analia's Bane Alley Blackguard. Changing which player controls an Aura or the enchanted object doesn’t by itself remove attachments; the Aura remains attached (see that an Aura’s controller is separate from the enchanted object’s controller: [303.4e]; and the Lay Claim ruling clarifies that effects that change control don’t cause attached Auras to move and that an Aura’s “you” refers to its controller: [Lay Claim ruling #0]).

Assumption: I assume the timing is as stated—Lay Claim resolved and became attached to Corrupted Conscience. If instead Lay Claim had been countered or otherwise failed to enter the battlefield, the control-change wouldn’t occur (resolution assumption).
entries.answer_gold: Analia controls both permanents. Out of the two auras, Corrupted Conscience has the earlier timestamp, and would normally be applied first. However, the effects from both auras apply in the same layer, applying the Lay Claim's effect would change how the Corrupted Conscience's effect is applied, and applying the Corrupted Conscience's effect would not change how the Lay Claim's effect is applied, so the Corrupted Conscience's effect is dependent on the Lay Claim's effect. The Lay Claim's effect applies first, giving Analia control of Corrupted Conscience, and then the Corrupted Conscience's effect applies, giving Analia control of Bane Alley Blackguard.

entries.question: Nathanael controls [Grizzly Bears] and [Muraganda Petroglyphs]. They cast and resolve [Crowd's Favor], targeting Grizzly Bears. Amia then casts [Archetype of Courage]. After it resolves, what are the power and toughness of Grizzly Bears?
entries.reason: The candidate reaches the same final ruling (Grizzly Bears is 5/4) and its layer/timestamp explanation matches the reference's conclusion.
entries.answer:
After Archetype of Courage resolves, Grizzly Bears is a 5/4.

Reasoning (stepwise):
- Grizzly Bears’s printed power and toughness are 2/2 (see rule 302.4c).  Muraganda Petroglyphs has the static ability “Creatures with no abilities get +2/+2,” which generates a continuous effect that modifies power/toughness while Muraganda Petroglyphs is on the battlefield (see Muraganda Petroglyphs and rules 611.3b and 613.1g). Initially, because Grizzly Bears had no abilities, Muraganda Petroglyphs would make Grizzly Bears a 4/4.
- When Crowd's Favor resolved earlier, it created two continuous effects: one that gives the targeted creature +1/+0 until end of turn (a power/toughness modifier applied in layer 7c) and one that gives that creature first strike until end of turn (an ability-adding effect applied in layer 6) (see Crowd's Favor and rule 613.4c and 613.6). While Grizzly Bears had first strike from Crowd's Favor, it did not satisfy “Creatures with no abilities,” so the Muraganda Petroglyphs bonus did not apply; Grizzly Bears would thus have been 3/2 (2/2 +1/+0) while it still had first strike.
- After Archetype of Courage resolves, Archetype of Courage’s continuous effect causes creatures its controller’s opponents control to lose first strike and to be unable to have or gain first strike (that effect is an ability-changing continuous effect applied in layer 6). Because Archetype of Courage’s effect has a later timestamp (it resolved after Crowd's Favor), in layer 6 it removes the first strike that Crowd's Favor had given Grizzly Bears (see Archetype of Courage and rules 613.7 and 613.6).
- Once that first-strike ability is removed, Grizzly Bears again has no abilities, so Muraganda Petroglyphs’s +2/+2 applies again in layer 7c. In layer 7c both Muraganda Petroglyphs’s +2/+2 and Crowd's Favor’s +1/+0 are applied (timestamps determine order within the sublayer but both are modifiers and thus both apply). The result is base 2/2 +2/+2 +1/+0 = 5/4.

Key term definitions used above:
- Continuous effect: a game effect generated (for example) by a static ability that applies as long as the object generating it is in the appropriate zone; such effects can modify characteristics like power and toughness (see rules 611.3b and 611.3c).
- Layers and timestamps: The game applies continuous effects by the layer system (power/toughness changes happen in layer 7), and within a layer or sublayer effects are ordered by timestamp unless dependency overrides that (see rules 613.1g, 613.4c, and 613.7). This is why ability changes in layer 6 (first strike being added or removed) affect whether a “no abilities” condition is true before layer 7c applies power/toughness modifiers (see rule 613.6).

Assumption about timing: I assumed the timeline given (Crowd's Favor resolved first, then Archetype of Courage resolved). If Archetype of Courage had been on the battlefield before Crowd's Favor resolved, then the “can't have or gain first strike” part of Archetype of Courage would have prevented Crowd's Favor from ever giving Grizzly Bears first strike; in that case Muraganda Petroglyphs would continuously give +2/+2 while Crowd's Favor would only add +1/+0, also producing a 5/4 result. (The cited layer/timestamp rules cover both orders.)
entries.answer_gold: 5/4. In layer 6, Archetype of Courage makes Crowd's Favor unable to grant first strike to Grizzly Bears. Archetype of Courage isn't granting any abilities to Grizzly Bears itself, so in layer 7 Grizzly Bears has no abilities and gets +2/+2 from Muraganda Petroglyphs and +1/+0 from Crowd's Favor.

If the order had been different (for example, if Life and Limb entered after Blood Moon), the timestamp situation could change which subtype-setting effect “wins,” and that could change whether Murmuring Bosk ends up a Forest and thus a creature. Fleetfeather Sandals’s static ability that says “Equipped creature has flying and haste” creates a continuous effect that grants flying when Fleetfeather Sandals becomes attached to Wandering Ones. When effects add and remove the same ability, the most recent continuous effect prevails; which effect is “most recent” is determined by timestamps (the later timestamp wins). An Aura or Equipment receives a new timestamp when it becomes attached to a creature, so Fleetfeather Sandals’s granting effect will have a later timestamp when you equip it after Tightening Coils is already attached, and therefore Wandering Ones ends up with flying. This outcome is also stated explicitly by the ruling on Tightening Coils: “If an effect gives the enchanted creature flying after Tightening Coils became attached to it, the creature will have flying.”

If instead Fleetfeather Sandals had been attached first and Tightening Coils became attached afterward, Tightening Coils’s later removal would make Wandering Ones lose flying.

Key term definitions:
- “Loses flying” means the effect removes the flying ability from the object (an ability-removing continuous effect).
- “Has” or “gains” flying means a continuous effect adds the flying ability to the object.
- A timestamp is the ordering marker used to determine which continuous effect applies last when multiple effects in the same layer add or remove the same ability; an Aura or Equipment gets a new timestamp each time it becomes attached.

Therefore the final characteristics while Titania's Song’s continuous effect applies: Soldevi Digger is an artifact and a creature (an artifact creature), with P/T 2/2 (its mana value), no abilities, and not an Equipment. Its mana value remains 2.

Assumption about timing: I am assuming Titania's Song has resolved after Bludgeon Brawl was already on the battlefield (the scenario you described). entries.question: Ariah controls [Wayward Angel] and has 7 cards in their graveyard. Nickolas casts [Turn to Frog], targeting Wayward Angel. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics after Turn to Frog resolves?

- Base power and base toughness are the values that count as a creature’s “base” numbers for later modifications; they are the numbers printed on the card unless an effect sets them to specific values (see rule 208.4a and rule 302.4c).
- To determine characteristics you start with the card’s printed values and then apply continuous effects in the layer system (see rules 613.1 and 613.1g).
- Turn to Frog’s effect includes several parts: it makes the target “become a blue Frog,” it sets the creature’s base power and toughness to 1/1, and it makes the target “lose all abilities.” Those parts apply in the appropriate layers (for example, color/type changes in their layer, base power/toughness setting in layer 7b, and gaining/losing abilities in layer 6); different parts of the same effect apply in different layers (see rule 613.6).
- Wayward Angel’s threshold static ability (already active because Ariah has seven cards in the graveyard) is a continuous effect that gives “+3/+3,” makes Wayward Angel black, and grants trample and a triggered upkeep ability. The “gets +3/+3” part is a power/toughness modifying effect (layer 7c), the color change is a color-changing effect, and the granted trample/triggered ability are granted abilities (see rule 113.12 and examples in 613.6).
- Timestamp order determines which continuous effects that apply in the same layer overwrite earlier ones (see rule 613.7). Turn to Frog resolved after Wayward Angel’s threshold was already in effect, so Turn to Frog’s color change and base-power-setting have later timestamps and apply after the earlier effects.
- Turn to Frog’s text explicitly “becomes a blue Frog with base power and toughness 1/1.” The Turn to Frog ruling #0 says Turn to Frog overwrites previous effects that set the creature’s base power and toughness to specific values; therefore Turn to Frog sets Wayward Angel’s base P/T to 1/1 (overwriting any prior P/T-setting). The threshold’s +3/+3 is a modifier (not a base-setting), so it still applies on top of the new base (see rules 208.4a, 613.4b, and 613.4c/7c ordering implied by 613.1g and 613.6). So base 1/1 +3/+3 = final 4/4.
- Turn to Frog makes the target “lose all abilities,” so the printed abilities (flying, vigilance) and the threshold-granted abilities (trample and the upkeep-triggered ability) are removed by that effect (see rule 113.12 distinguishing setting characteristics and granted abilities). Turn to Frog ruling #3 notes that if a creature gains an ability after Turn to Frog resolves it will keep that ability; that is not happening here, so Wayward Angel has no abilities while Turn to Frog’s effect lasts.
- Concerning color: Wayward Angel ruling #0 says that when you have seven or more cards in your graveyard Wayward Angel is black (not white). However, Turn to Frog’s color-changing part is a later continuous effect that makes the creature blue; later timestamped color-changing effects overwrite earlier ones in the same layer (see rule 613.7 and rule 613.6). Therefore the creature is blue while Turn to Frog’s effect lasts (not black or white).
- For type/subtype: Turn to Frog’s text makes the creature “become a ... Frog.” As Turn to Frog changes the creature type in its layer and has a later timestamp, the creature will be a Frog creature while Turn to Frog’s effect lasts (see Turn to Frog ruling #4 for an example of how Turn to Frog replaces creature types).

Assumption: I assume there is no other effect or subsequent timestamped effect affecting Wayward Angel before you check its characteristics. If another later effect sets power/toughness or grants abilities after Turn to Frog resolves, that later effect could change the final values (Turn to Frog ruling #0 and rule 613.7 explain later effects overwrite earlier ones when they apply in the same layer).

It's removed by Turn to Frog in layer 6, but since it's already started to apply, it will continue doing so in later layers. entries.question: Natalie controls [High Fae Trickster]. Allen activates the crew ability of [Capenna Express]. Before it resolves Natalie casts [One with the Stars] targeting Capenna Express. What happens when the crew ability resolves?
entries.reason: The candidate says One with the Stars fizzles and is put into the graveyard before the crew resolves, whereas the reference says the Aura resolved and both type-changing effects apply (with the crew ability winning by timestamp), so they reach different final outcomes.
entries.answer:
One with the Stars is put into its owner’s graveyard without entering the battlefield, and then the crew ability resolves and Capenna Express becomes an artifact creature until end of turn (crewed by High Fae Trickster if High Fae Trickster was tapped to pay the crew cost). 

Why: When One with the Stars tries to resolve as an Aura spell it checks whether its target is still legal; One with the Stars can only enchant a creature or an enchantment, and Capenna Express is currently a noncreature artifact, so the target is illegal and the Aura spell doesn’t resolve (it’s put into its owner’s graveyard instead of entering the battlefield) [608.3b, 608.2b, 303.4i]. After that, the already-activated crew ability resolves: Crew N is an activated ability that makes the Vehicle become an artifact creature until end of turn when its crew cost is paid; a creature “crews a Vehicle” when it was tapped to pay that crew cost [702.122a, 702.122b, 702.122c]. 

Definitions relied on: 
- “Crewing” / “crewed”: A Vehicle is crewed by a creature if that creature was tapped to pay the cost to activate that Vehicle’s crew ability; “Crew N” is an activated ability that taps creatures with total power N or more to make the Vehicle an artifact creature until end of turn [702.122a, 702.122b, 702.122c]. 
- “Illegal target” (for a resolving spell): A spell that specifies targets checks whether those targets are still legal as it begins to resolve; if all of its targets are illegal, the spell doesn’t resolve and is put into its owner’s graveyard (special rules apply for bestowed Auras and mutating creature spells, which don’t apply here) [608.2b, 608.3b]. 

Note on a different timing: If One with the Stars had been cast (or resolved) after Capenna Express had already become an artifact creature, One with the Stars could legally enchant Capenna Express while it was a creature; One with the Stars’s effect could then cause the enchanted Capenna Express to be an enchantment and lose other card types (see One with the Stars ruling #1) [One with the Stars ruling #1].
entries.answer_gold: Capenna Express will become an artifact creature as normal. One with the Stars and Capenna Express's abilities both apply in layer 4 and attempt to change its type. Capenna Express's ability will have the newer timestamp, and it resolved most recently. ([613.7], [613.7b], [702.122a])

entries.question: Nico controls [Humility]. Aitana casts [Finale of Devastation] with X = 10. Will the creature they find have haste?
entries.reason: Both answers conclude effects apply in layer 6 and, due to timestamp order, Finale's later continuous effect grants haste so the creature will have haste.
entries.answer: Yes — the creature Finale of Devastation finds will have haste (until end of turn). Finale of Devastation with X = 10 creates a continuous effect that gives creatures you control +X/+X and haste; the official ruling says the creature you put onto the battlefield “will get +X/+X and haste” when X is 10 or more, and that nothing happens between revealing the card and it getting those effects ([Finale of Devastation ruling #2]; [Finale of Devastation ruling #0]). Humility’s static ability makes “All creatures lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 1/1” (Humility). When effects add and remove abilities, the more recent continuous effect generally prevails ([113.10c]; [113.10]). Because the continuous effect from Finale of Devastation is created when Finale resolves (after Humility is already on the battlefield), that later effect grants haste to the creature as it enters. Also, continuous effects that apply to an entering permanent are applied as it enters, so the haste from Finale will be present as the creature enters the battlefield ([611.3]; [613.1]). Haste is a static ability ([702.10a]) that lets the creature’s controller activate its activated abilities whose cost includes the tap or untap symbol and lets it attack despite the “summoning sickness” restriction ([702.10c]). Assumption: Humility was already on the battlefield before Finale resolved; if Humility instead entered after Finale’s effect was created, timestamps and layer interactions would need to be checked (the most recent continuous effect would still generally determine whether the creature ends up with haste).
entries.answer_gold: Yes. Both effects apply in layer 6, and are applied in timestamp order. Since Finale of Devastation's effect has the most recent timestamp, it's applied last.

entries.question: Aubree casts [Blood Moon]. Nikolas activates [Inkmoth Nexus]'s ability in response. What will Inkmoth Nexus look like after everything resolves? What will it look like next turn?
entries.reason: Both answers conclude Inkmoth Nexus will be a 1/1 Artifact Land Creature - Mountain Blinkmoth with flying, infect and gain Mountain’s "{T}: Add {R}" (losing its printed mana ability) while the pump lasts, and will revert next turn to just a Mountain land with "{T}: Add {R}".
entries.answer:
After both spells/abilities resolve, Inkmoth Nexus is a 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature with flying and infect and is also a land with the land type Mountain; it has the Mountain mana ability “{T}: Add {R}” and has lost its printed “{T}: Add {C}” ability. Next turn (after the “until end of turn” effect from Inkmoth Nexus’s activated ability ends), Inkmoth Nexus will be just a land with land type Mountain that has “{T}: Add {R}” (it will no longer be an artifact or creature, and will no longer have flying, infect, or be 1/1).

Reasoning and assumptions (short): I assume Nikolas’s activation resolved first because it was activated in response to Aubree casting Blood Moon; that puts the continuous effect from Inkmoth Nexus’s activated ability on the stack first and gives it the earlier timestamp when it begins applying (but the final result is the same whichever resolved first, because both continuous effects will be applied in layer 4 and Blood Moon’s later-applied effect will set the land type to Mountain). Layer and ability interactions: the Inkmoth Nexus activated ability makes “This land becomes a 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature with flying and infect until end of turn. It’s still a land,” which is a type-changing/ability-adding continuous effect applied in layer 4 (see rule 613.1d and the example in 613.6). An effect that sets a land’s subtype to a basic land type (Blood Moon’s effect) causes the land to lose its old land types and lose abilities generated from its rules text, and to gain the new basic land type’s mana ability; it doesn’t remove abilities granted by other effects (see rule 305.7 and Blood Moon ruling #2). Because Inkmoth Nexus’s activated ability’s continuous effect already exists, it continues to make Inkmoth Nexus an artifact creature with flying, infect, and P/T 1/1 until end of turn even though Blood Moon causes the land to lose its printed mana ability (613.6 and 305.7). Blood Moon therefore replaces Inkmoth Nexus’s land subtype with Mountain and gives “{T}: Add {R}” (Blood Moon ruling #2); the printed “{T}: Add {C}” is removed because it was generated from Inkmoth Nexus’s rules text (305.7). When the until-end-of-turn effect from Inkmoth Nexus’s activated ability expires on the next turn, the artifact and creature types and the flying/infect and 1/1 setting end, leaving Inkmoth Nexus as a Mountain that has “{T}: Add {R}.”

If the timing were reversed (Blood Moon resolves before the activated ability resolves), the same final state after both have resolved obtains: Inkmoth Nexus would still end up a 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature with flying and infect and land type Mountain while the activated ability’s effect lasts, then revert to being a Mountain that produces {R} on the next turn.
entries.answer_gold: Inkmoth Nexus will be a 1/1 Artifact Land Creature - Mountain Blinkmoth with flying, infect, {T}: Add {R}, and no other abilities. Next turn it will be a Land - Mountain with {T}: Add {R} and no other abilities. Setting a land's subtype to a basic land type causes it to lose all other land types, as well as all abilities granted by its rules text, and gain the appropriate mana ability from its new land type. It will still keep abilities granted to it by other effects as those are gained in layer 6 while Blood Moon's type-changing effect applies in layer 4, so it will still have flying and infect. Removing the activated ability from Inkmoth Nexus does not affect the instance of the ability that has already resolved, so the effect will end as normal and Inkmoth Nexus will not be a creature next turn.

entries.question: Niko controls [Urza's Saga] on chapter 2. Ainsley casts [Magus of the Moon]. What happens to Urza's Saga?
entries.reason: The candidate reaches the same final ruling: Urza's Saga becomes a Mountain and gains "{T}: Add {R}" while keeping the chapter I and II abilities it already gained, will not get further lore counters, and is not sacrificed.
entries.answer:
Urza's Saga becomes a Mountain (losing its Urza’s land subtype) but keeps the chapter I and II abilities it gained earlier and also gains the Mountain mana ability. In short: Urza's Saga is affected by Magus of the Moon, becomes a Mountain and therefore has “{T}: Add {R},” yet Urza's Saga still keeps its chapter-granted “{T}: Add {C}” and “{2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct…” abilities, so it is not immediately sacrificed by this change.

Reasoning and definitions:
- Magus of the Moon’s continuous effect makes nonbasic lands Mountains, so any nonbasic land Niko controls becomes a Mountain when Magus of the Moon is on the battlefield (this is a subtype-setting effect) ([305.7]; [Magus of the Moon ruling #0]).
- By “nonbasic land” here I mean a land that does not already have one of the basic land types Plains/Island/Swamp/Mountain/Forest (the basic land types are listed in rule [305.6]).
- When a land’s subtype is set to a basic land type, that land gains the appropriate intrinsic mana ability for that basic land type (a Mountain gives “{T}: Add {R}”) ([305.6]; [305.7]). Therefore Urza's Saga gains “{T}: Add {R}.”
- Rule [305.7] normally causes a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type to lose abilities generated from its rules text, but the official ruling for Urza's Saga states that “Urza's Saga gains an ability from its first and second chapters. It keeps those abilities for as long as it's on the battlefield.” Because that ruling is authoritative for Urza's Saga, Urza's Saga keeps the chapter I and II abilities it already gained while on the battlefield (Urza's Saga ruling #5). As a result Urza's Saga still has the chapter I ability “{T}: Add {C}” and the chapter II ability “{2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct…”.
- If at some later time Urza's Saga did actually lose all of its chapter abilities while still a Saga (for example, due to a different effect that removes those abilities), Urza's Saga would be sacrificed immediately per the official ruling ([Urza's Saga ruling #1]). Also note that Urza's Saga is still a Saga while it is a land, and it will be sacrificed after its last chapter ability resolves as described by its ruling ([Urza's Saga ruling #4]).
entries.answer_gold:
It becomes an Enchantment Land - Saga Mountain with an ability to tap for {R}, an ability to tap for {1}, an ability to create Constructs, and no other abilities.

Since it no longer has any chapter abilities, it will remain at 2 lore counters and will not receive any more in future turns. It is not sacrificed.

entries.answer:

Reasoning: “Color” means the color or colors of the mana symbols in an object’s mana cost (and can be changed by effects) ([202.2], [105.2], [105.3]). That ability adds blue to objects that already have colors and makes normally colorless objects the chosen color (Painter's Servant ruling #5; Painter's Servant ruling #0). Painter's Servant has no colored mana symbols in its mana cost, so Painter's Servant would be colorless except for its own chosen-color effect; because of Painter's Servant’s effect and ruling #0, Painter's Servant becomes blue (not “colorless and blue”) once the choice is made. If Painter's Servant entered after Dress Down was cast, Painter's Servant’s characteristic-defining ability will apply once Painter's Servant’s choice exists and will make the spell blue as described (Painter's Servant; [604.3]).

entries.question: Anabella controls [Blood Moon] and enchants their [Sunlit Marsh] with [Urban Utopia]. What colors can it tap for?
entries.reason: Both conclude the land retains Urban Utopia’s {T}: Add one mana of any color while also being a Mountain with {T}: Add {R}, so you can produce any color.
entries.answer:
Sunlit Marsh can be tapped to add one mana of any color (via Urban Utopia) or to add {R} (as a Mountain created by Blood Moon). 

Reasoning: "To ‘tap [a permanent] for mana’" means to activate a mana ability that includes {T} in its activation cost (definition from rule [106.12b]). Blood Moon makes nonbasic lands Mountains and gives them the ability "{T}: Add {R}" (see Blood Moon ruling #2 and the basic land/mountain rule [305.6]), and in doing so a nonbasic land loses abilities generated from its rules text per rule [305.7] (so Sunlit Marsh’s printed "{T}: Add {W} or {B}." is lost). Urban Utopia grants the enchanted land the ability "{T}: Add one mana of any color," and the Urban Utopia ruling #0 states the enchanted land won’t lose other abilities it had because of that aura; in particular the ability Urban Utopia grants remains (and 305.7 does not remove abilities granted by other effects). Because Sunlit Marsh therefore has both the Urban Utopia granted ability and the Mountain ability from Blood Moon, you may choose to activate either one when you tap Sunlit Marsh: Urban Utopia’s ability can produce any color (white, blue, black, red, or green), while the Mountain ability produces {R}. Note that each is a {T}-activation, so tapping Sunlit Marsh to activate one of them prevents activating the other until Sunlit Marsh becomes untapped ([106.12b]).
entries.answer_gold: Any color. Blood Moon operates in the type-changing layer which is applied before the ability adding and removing layer. Sunlit Marsh is a Mountain, with the additional ability "{T}: Add one mana of any color.".
